mm-terrarium · front end audit & design brief

The Terrarium Console

Everything the venue operator panel does today, what it does badly, and the Musical Mycology tokens to rebuild it against. Written to be handed to a designer.

audited 2026-08-25 · branch claude/terrarium-web-audit-084bcc

01What it is

A Bit-agnostic local admin panel: the one surface an operator uses to pick a Bit, start it, watch it, intervene in it, and stop it. It renders whatever the loaded Bit declares, and knows nothing about any particular Bit.

Served by
ConsoleServerconsole/server.py

Framework
Noneno build, no deps

One portHTTP + websocket

None127.0.0.1, trusted LAN
Panels
9stacked, one column
Wire
6 up / 13 downJSON over websocket

Starting it

.venv/bin/python -m harness.terrarium_boot --console-port 8772

Off by default. --console-port with neither --seconds nor --hold implies --serve, which loops rounds rather than tearing down after the first Bit completes.

The four static files

FileLinesRole
index.html45Page skeleton: nine sections, four empty tables, four empty divs
console.js174Websocket, event dispatch, Bits panel, the three tables, event log
room.js237Room panel: fixture LED strips, zone bars, instrument cards
triggers.js168Trigger cards, Fire buttons, device pickers
style.css53Every style on the page

room.js and triggers.js are IIFE-wrapped and export exactly their entry points onto window. That is not stylistic. A shared buildCard helper in both files previously collided, triggers.js loaded second and silently won, and renderRoom threw on every room_changed. Any overhaul must preserve that isolation or replace it with a module system.

Scope. This is the only web front end mm-terrarium owns. The browser canvases you see during a run, one per simulated Tuneshroom and one per Room fixture, are luxaeterna's WebSimBackend and are out of scope.

02What it looks like now

Both captured from the real console with no code changes, driven by a scratch harness that builds GameServer, ConsoleServer and ConsoleAgent directly. No Arco, no simulator subprocess, no o2lite.

03The nine panels

In DOM order, top to bottom. Every one of these is a function the rebuild has to carry forward in some form.

Header

#conn

The only connection indicator: connecting, connected, or disconnected, retrying in red. Reconnect is a flat 1 s retry with no backoff and no attempt counter.

Bits

#bits · bits_listed

Loaded Bit and state on one line, then Run and Abort, then one card per discovered bits/*/bit.toml: display name, kind badge, version, room types, start condition, description, Load. Hidden Bits render at 50% opacity but stay loadable. Red-bordered error cards carry the path and parse error.

Room

#room · room_changed, room_frame

A header line, then one live LED strip per fixture (one div per pixel, 864 of them on DEMO) with a proportional zone bar underneath, then one card per declared instrument. Light and audio share one list, discriminated by badge. Each lane reads cc:74 → hue = 93, where the number is live.

Triggers

#triggers · triggers_changed, trigger_fired

One card per declared trigger: name, DEVICE/ROOM badge, description, the condition and its source, every script step as a monospace line, a device picker for DEVICE targets, a Fire button, and a last-fired line. An admin-manual fire is tagged ADMIN MANUAL in amber so an operator action never reads as gameplay.

Registration

#registration

Role, count, capacity. Unbounded renders as ∞. The Room's own role is filtered out before it reaches the browser.

Roles & media manifests

#roles

Role, class, capacity, scored, and both manifests as raw JSON.stringify output inside a table cell.

Devices

#devices · devices_changed

Device id, friendly name, role. Every device that has said hello, whether or not it holds a role. A device bound as the Room appears with its role blanked.

Bit status

#bitStatus · bit_status

Whatever Bit.status() returns, one row per key, untyped, stringified by assignment to textContent.

Event log

#log

An 8rem scrolling monospace box. Append-only, auto-scrolled. State transitions, bit completions, errors, and server-pushed log lines, each prefixed [info] or [error].

04Wire protocol

Six commands go up, thirteen events come down. Three of the six commands are fully implemented server-side and have no button anywhere in the UI.

Browser to server

CommandPayloadHas UISent by
run—yesRun button
abort—yesAbort button
load_bitname, overrides?partialLoad button, never with overrides
fire_triggername, dev?yesFire buttons
list_bits—noneNothing sends it
arm_roomroom_type, fixture, window_secondsnoneNothing sends it
release_roomroom_type, fixture?noneNothing sends it

fire_trigger, arm_room and release_room are console-only admin commands, parsed separately from the shared uplink parser on purpose, so a remote fairyring peer can never request them.

Server to browser

EventWhenPanel
snapshotOnce on connect, the full read modelAll
bits_listedOnce on connectBits
state_changedEvery lifecycle transitionBits header, log
registration_changedEvery join and leaveRegistration
devices_changedEvery hello and reapDevices, trigger pickers
bit_statusOn change, checked per tickBit status
room_changedOn change, includes live controller valuesRoom
room_frameDecimated to ~10 Hz, one per fixture (bound or not)Room strips
triggers_changedOn change, in practice load and unloadTriggers
trigger_firedPer fireTrigger status lines
bit_completedOn UNLOADING, if result is not NoneLog
errorPer refused commandLog
logServer-pushedLog

Room frames are droppable by design. The Room renders at 44 Hz; the console is a monitor and gets roughly 10, with intermediate frames overwritten rather than queued, keyed per fixture name. Nothing gameplay waits on may ever be put behind this panel.

05Rendering rules that must survive

Each of these is the fix for a defect found on live hardware. A rewrite that loses one re-introduces the bug.

  1. A high-frequency event must never rebuild a list. Bits, Triggers and the Room fixture strips are rebuilt only when their declared shape changes, gated on a JSON signature. state_changed fires continuously; room_frame fires ten times a second.
  2. A frame paints, it does not rebuild. renderRoomFrame writes swatch background colours and nothing else.
  3. Rebuild granularity is per fixture, not per Room. An untouched fixture's live strip must survive another fixture's reconfiguration.
  4. Declaration order is physical order. A rebuilt fixture is reinserted in place, before the nearest later surviving fixture, never appended.
  5. Pending frames are keyed per device. A single slot starved every fixture but the last one to render in a tick.
  6. The wire is GRB. Decoding it as RGB renders every zone the wrong colour, which looks like a lighting design decision rather than a bug.
  7. No shared globals between panel scripts.
  8. The Room's node id, role name and registration counts stay hidden while its instruments, surface and live values stay visible. That split is tested in both directions.
  9. An unknown device in a frame event is a no-op, not an error. Frames can race a Room reconfiguration.

06What is wrong with it

Fourteen findings, graded by how much each one costs at a venue. The grading is the structure: the first four are the ones that make the panel hard to operate during a show.

Hurts most Missing affordance Quality of life
  • 01 Light mode only, and pinned to it

    The stylesheet hard-codes background-color: #fff behind an eight-line comment explaining that the palette is built for a light background and that a real dark theme is a separate design decision. The Terrarium is a dark room. This is the single biggest mismatch between the panel and where it is used.

  • 02 Trigger cards are unbounded in height

    Every script step renders as a flat monospace line. MetronomeBit's fireworks_player script is 36 steps, so one card is taller than the viewport and the Triggers section alone runs about 900 px. There is no collapse, no summary, no timeline.

  • 03 No state gating on controls

    Run and Abort are enabled in every state. The console offers an illegal transition, the engine refuses it, and the refusal appears as a red line in the event log after the fact. There is no confirmation on Abort.

  • 04 Manifests are raw JSON in a table cell

    light_manifest in the Roles table is one JSON.stringify string wrapping across three lines. The Room panel already proves the readable version exists, with badges, params and live lane values. The Roles table just does not use it.

  • 05 Room binding has no UI

    arm_room and release_room are fully implemented, are the only way a fixture gets bound to a device at a venue, and have no button. Today they are reachable only by hand-crafting a websocket frame.

  • 06 Bit configuration has no UI

    load_bit accepts an overrides dict, the agent resolves it through BitRegistry.resolve_config, and a bad key comes back as a clean located error. The UI never sends one, so retuning MetronomeBit's bpm at a venue means editing a profile TOML and restarting.

  • 07 Devices show no liveness

    Device, name, role, and nothing else. No last-seen, no protoversion, no signal, even though reap_stale silently drops a device after 15 s of silence and frees its role slot.

  • 08 Registration shows counts, not occupancy

    Who holds which slot lives in a different table two sections away.

  • 09 The event log is a textContent accumulator

    No cap, no timestamps, no filtering, no severity colour beyond the bracketed prefix, no way to copy one line. It grows unbounded for the life of the tab.

  • 10 Trigger fire history is broadcast-only

    trigger_fired is not part of snapshot, so a browser opened after a fire shows never fired for a trigger that has been firing all night.

  • 11 No responsive layout

    There is a viewport meta tag and nothing else. Tables and trigger cards overflow horizontally on a tablet, which is the form factor an operator actually walks the room with.

  • 12 Bit.status() is untyped

    An empty list renders as an empty cell (see tap_errors_ms in the screenshot). A nested dict would render as [object Object].

  • 13 No brand identity at all

    System font stack, browser-default buttons, no favicon, no logo, no Musical Mycology colour anywhere. It looks like a debug page because it is one.

  • 14 The 864 pixel strip is 864 DOM nodes

    It works, and it is the heaviest thing on the page. A canvas would be one node.

07Design system: the tension to resolve

Build a dark-surface variant of the existing MM system, not a new system and not a straight light-mode port.

The brand already sanctions dark surfaces and already specifies what accents do there: --mm-mushroom for dark cards, --mm-dark-brown for the deepest surface, and --mm-gold used only on dark. So a dark console is an existing, documented branch of the system rather than a departure from it. Cream becomes the ink, mushroom-brown becomes the surface, gold becomes the accent. This page is built that way, so you can see the branch running.

Supporting: the console's own CSS already defers this decision in a comment; and a full-brightness cream panel next to a 6 m LED array wrecks the operator's dark adaptation and washes out the room. What would change the call: if the console ends up mostly used on a tablet in daylight during setup rather than at the back of a dark room during a show, the light cream system is the better fit as-is.

The MM design system was built for a marketing website and a pitch deck. Its whole premise is warm cream paper, generous air, and slow motion. The console is an operator panel read at a glance, in the dark, while a show is running. Those two want opposite things, and three specifics have to be negotiated rather than inherited.

The system has no status palette. There is no defined success, warning, error or running colour. The console needs one for state badges, error rows, the ADMIN MANUAL tag and the connection indicator. Sage reads as go and rose as fail, but both are marked rare in the brand doc, so promoting them to a recurring status role is a real extension and should be an explicit decision. This page does exactly that, in its severity stripes and its yes/no chips, as a proposal.

Type

RoleFamilyWhere
DisplayLondrina Solid
100 / 300 / 400 / 900		Titles, eyebrows, the subtitle bar, button labels. Never paragraphs.
BodyAtkinson Hyperlegible
400 / 700 + italics		Paragraph copy, captions, and any UI label longer than about three words
Dataui-monospace, SF Mono, MenloNot a brand face. The console leans hard on it: cue scripts, the log, manifests, controller values

Eyebrows: uppercase, terracotta (gold on dark), 0.78rem, 0.2em tracking. The console's existing LIGHT / AUDIO / TOOL / R_GAME / DEVICE / ROOM badges are already eyebrow-shaped and are the natural place to land this.

Geometry and shadow

Spacing   4 / 8 / 12 / 16 / 24 / 32 / 48 / 64 / 80 / 128
Radii     xs 4px subtitle bar · sm 10px badges · md 16px hero card
          lg 18px inner cards · xl 20px section boxes · pill 9999px
Borders   1.5px default · 2.5px outline buttons · warm tan, never grey
Shadows   card    0 3px 16px  rgba(92,61,46,0.07)
          lift    0 14px 40px rgba(92,61,46,0.16)
          slide   0 12px 48px rgba(58,35,24,0.13)
Motion    fast 0.2s · med 0.45s · reveal 0.7s · float 6s · spore 18s
          ease cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1) · soft cubic-bezier(0.25,1,0.5,1)

Shadows are warm and brown-tinted, never neutral grey. No inner shadows, no gradient borders, no neumorphism. Muted is achieved by lowering the opacity of brown over cream, never by reaching for grey.

Two more places the brand does not cover an operator panel

  • Density. The brand specifies ~80px section padding and a 1060px centred column, described as vertical and breathing. A dashboard is the opposite. Keep the radii, warm borders, warm shadows and type roles; compress the spacing scale by about one step and let the content run wider.
  • Motion budget. Brand motion is 0.7s reveals and 6s float cycles. A panel whose job is to report state changes the instant they happen wants 0.2s or nothing. Reserve the slow motion for decoration, and probably run none at all on the live LED strip.

Imagery

Mushroom PNG illustrations are the brand's icon set, cartoon-naturalist, used as corner ornaments at 0.1 to 0.35 opacity. Never hand-draw new mushroom SVGs; copy the PNGs. Assets live on the design-assets CDN, and every day_* asset has a night_* counterpart, which is directly relevant to a dark console. The brand has no functional icon set and recommends Lucide as a flagged substitution; the console needs play, stop, fire, link, warning and chevron, so that decision is forced by this overhaul.

One caution: corner mushrooms at low opacity are the brand's signature texture, and they compete with an 864 pixel live LED strip for exactly the same visual attention. Likely answer: identity in the header only, and nothing decorative below it.

08Open decisions

Seven calls this overhaul forces, because the brand as written does not yet cover what an operator panel needs.

DecisionRecommendation
Light or dark surfaceDark, on mushroom-brown and dark-brown with gold as the accent
Status palettePromote sage and rose out of "rare" into recurring status roles
DensityBrand radii, borders, shadows and type; spacing compressed one step; full width
Functional iconsLucide, as the system already recommends, but confirm it
Monospace faceChoose one deliberately; the console leans on it and it is not a brand face
Motion budget0.2s or instant for anything carrying state; slow motion for decoration only
DecorationIdentity in the header, nothing decorative below it

09What a rebuild must not break

  • The engine seam. ConsoleAgent attaches through GameServer's multi-observer list and is driven by poll() from the tick loop. Nothing in the front end may become something gameplay waits on.
  • The single-port model. One server hands out static assets and the websocket on the same listener, behind an extension allowlist with basename-only path resolution. Adding a build step means deciding how built assets reach that allowlist.
  • Offline testability. console/protocol.py, control/room_view.py and control/trigger_view.py are pure dict builders with no engine imports, and the whole panel is tested against an in-process fake with no socket. Six test files cover it.
  • The shared protocol builders. state_changed, registration_changed, bit_completed, bits_listed and error are byte-identical between the console and the outbound uplink, on purpose.
  • The trust model, unless authentication lands at the same time. The moment this panel faces an untrusted network, auth is a prerequisite and not an enhancement.
